newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to meet Israel's President Weizman.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to meet Israel's President Weizman.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman will host Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at his home in the Jewish state on Tuesday, Weizman said on Monday.
"Tomorrow will be the first time that I will sit with him in an organised fashion," Weizman said at a meeting of former Israeli parliamentarians.
Weizman said he had briefly met Arafat on two previous occasions -- the inauguration of South Africa's Nelson Mandela and the funeral of France's Francois Mitterand.
Israel Radio said Arafat would travel by helicopter to the Israeli town of Caesarea for the meeting with Weizman whose presidential role in Israel is largely ceremonial.
Weizman announced in August he would agree to Arafat's request for a meeting at a time when Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu still refused to set a date for talks with the Palestinian leader.
Netanyahu and Arafat met for the first time days later.
Legislator Rehavam Zeevi of the extreme right-wing Moledet party slammed Weizman for inviting Arafat, whom he compared with Adolf Hitler.
"In politics you can change your opinions but there's a big difference between that and hosting Adolf Arafat at home in Caesarea," Zeevi told Israel Radio.
Israelis and Palestinians resumed peace talks on Sunday after an outburst of violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip in which 58 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
